::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 13th 1867  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS John Rylands Library, Manchester, FA1/7/831
:::

[Sir](people/person_523.qmd),
I am afraid you will think your kind mention of the [Little Duke](cmy_books/cmybook_20.qmd) in your [history](other_books/otherbook_482.qmd) of the Norman Conquest[^1] has brought on you an infliction -

But I cannot resist the desire to send you my later story the [Prince and the Page](cmy_books/cmybook_61.qmd) because in it I have tried as far as the scope of the story would allow, to do justice to the character of Simon de Montfort and Edward I. I am aware that there is a very serious blunder owing to my having supposed that a Knight Hospitalier was necessarily also a priest, and I am also told that I was led astray by the temptation of interweaving the story of the Beggar of Bethnal Green; but on the whole I think it tends to bring out the character of that great hero whose fame you have been so thoroughly defending. And I cannot refuse myself the pleasure of thanking you for the clue you have given to that chaos of history before the Conquest

Yours faithfully
C. M.Yonge

---

[^1]: Freeman had written in his *History of the Norman conquest* I, 233:'I cannot help also mentioning Miss Yonge's tale of the ;Little Duke,' where the whole legend is very pleasantly told, though with too great a leaning to the Norman side.'
